blocks.content: Delhi's heritage chapter is exceptionally dense given its 'Seven Cities' history (Chapter 2) - this chapter focuses specifically on UNESCO World Heritage Sites and other flagship monuments most likely to be directly tested by name.
UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Delhi

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Study of UNESCO World Heritage Sites situated in Delhi.
Overview of other major architectural monuments and heritage landmarks.
Insight into prominent museums and national cultural institutions.
Quick revision sections structured for last-minute exam prep.

cells: Begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak (1199), completed by Iltutmish; Alai Darwaza added by Alauddin Khalji
Tallest brick minaret in the world (~73 m); inscribed 1993
Precursor to Taj Mahal's char-bagh design; inscribed 1993
Imperial residence of Shahjahanabad; site of PM's Independence Day flag-hoisting/address every 15 August; inscribed 2007

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Delhi has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites - Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb, and Red Fort Complex - all three drawn from the medieval/Mughal chapter (Chapter 2). The Prime Minister's Independence Day address from the Red Fort ramparts is a near-certain current-affairs-cum-heritage crossover fact.

cells: War memorial (originally commemorating Indian soldiers of WWI and the Third Anglo-Afghan War); designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens; site of the Amar Jawan Jyoti flame, now merged with the National War Memorial flame
Inaugurated 2019, near India Gate; commemorates Indian soldiers who died in post-Independence conflicts
Official residence of the President of India; designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens; formerly 'Viceroy's House'
Circular colonnaded building designed by Herbert Baker; seat of India's Parliament since Independence; a new Parliament building (built alongside) was inaugurated in 2023
Modern lotus-shaped Bahai temple, completed 1986, a major contemporary architectural landmark
Large modern Hindu temple complex on the Yamuna's east bank, inaugurated 2005, known for its craftsmanship and cultural exhibitions
Principal mosque of Shahjahanabad, built by Shah Jahan; one of India's largest mosques
Landscaped park containing tombs of Lodi and Sayyid dynasty rulers
Site traditionally associated with ancient Indraprastha; fort built by Humayun/Sher Shah Suri
Memorial/cremation site of Mahatma Gandhi on the Yamuna bank; a simple black marble platform

items: National Museum, New Delhi - India's largest museum, housing artefacts spanning prehistory to the modern era.
National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA) - premier institution for modern and contemporary Indian art.
Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) and the National Archives of India are key research/cultural institutions headquartered in Delhi.

Delhi hosts numerous major annual cultural events, including the Delhi International Arts Festival and various government-supported heritage walks and festivals centred on Old Delhi's living Mughal-era culture (cuisine, crafts, qawwali traditions around the Nizamuddin Dargah).
Identify which monuments in Delhi hold official UNESCO World Heritage status.
Match key museums and cultural institutions with their specific historical focus or location.
3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Delhi: Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb, Red Fort Complex.
India Gate (WWI memorial) and the newer National War Memorial (2019) both stand near each other; PM addresses the nation from the Red Fort every Independence Day.
Rashtrapati Bhavan and Sansad Bhavan are both British-era (Lutyens/Baker) landmark government buildings; a NEW Parliament building was inaugurated in 2023.
Lotus Temple (1986) and Akshardham Temple (2005) are Delhi's flagship modern religious/architectural landmarks.
